# rowfence

> Access rules for Postgres. A policy file (`.authz`) says who can do what; the `rowfence` command compiles it
> into row-level security, trigger-maintained tables for inheritance and `authz.*` SQL functions, and ships
> each change as a migration for the app's own tool (Alembic, Prisma, Drizzle Kit, SQL, goose, dbmate,
> Flyway). Any Postgres 16, 17 or 18; no extension, no superuser. SDKs for Python (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy) and
> TypeScript (Next.js, Prisma, Drizzle, pg, postgres.js, React).

What an agent needs to know:

- The policy lives in one file named by `rowfence.toml` (`policy = "db/policy.authz"`), with tests beside it
  (`tests = ["db/tests/*.authz"]`). Everything that grants access is written in the policy.
- The loop after editing it: `rowfence check` (the first mistake, with its line and a code like `[AZ201]`),
  `rowfence push` (the development database only), `rowfence test`. Or `rowfence dev`, which does all three on
  each save. `rowfence help AZ201` explains a code and shows the mistake fixed.
- Production takes migrations: `rowfence migrate` writes the next one from `db/policy.lock`; never `push`.
- App code checks nothing by hand. Each transaction signs in (`SELECT authz.act_as('user', '42')`, which the
  SDKs do), then plain queries are filtered, refused writes raise SQLSTATE 42501 with the reason (the SDKs
  answer 403), and rows the user can't see are 404.
- `rowfence mcp` is an MCP server with the command's tools: `check`, `prove`, `review`, `test`, `why`, `lint`
  and `push`.

A small policy:

```authz
app role app_user                               -- the Postgres role the app connects as
type user = app.users
type folder = app.folders
  owner  : user   = owner_id                    -- a relation read from a column
  parent : folder = parent_id
  editor : user   = app.folder_editors(folder_id -> user_id)   -- ... or from a link table
  can edit = owner or editor or parent.edit     -- inherited down the tree
  can view = edit
rules app.folders
  select : view
  update : edit
```

## Docs

- [The policy language](docs/reference/language.md): types, relations, permissions, inheritance, denies, rules, masks, invariants, tests
- [Using it from app code](docs/reference/app-code.md): every `authz.*` function, the generated clients, refusals that say why
- [Identity](docs/reference/identity.md): a trusted backend, API keys and scopes, JWTs, services; signed sessions
- [Governance](docs/reference/governance.md): audit trail, change feed, requests, break glass, reviews; `authz.lint()`
- [Tools](docs/reference/tools.md): every `rowfence` command, `rowfence.toml`, the MCP server
- [Migrations](docs/reference/migrations.md): a policy change as a migration for your tool, the lock file
- [Reviewing a change](docs/reference/review.md): what `rowfence review` says on a pull request
- [How it works](docs/reference/guarantees.md): what it compiles to, what it guarantees, security
- [Speed and limits](docs/reference/limits.md): measured speed, and what it doesn't do
- [Installing](docs/installing.md): npm, pip or the image; alphas and release candidates; from the repository
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): from a schema to a policy, tests, the dev loop and migrations (run as written by the tests)
- [Cookbook](docs/cookbook.md): tested patterns (teams inside teams, inheritance that stops, sharing for a while and share links, denies, tenants, bots, blocking, live updates)
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): what people run into, by what they see
- [Running rowfence](docs/operations.md): configuration, behind a pooler, deploying a change, upgrading, backups, retention, what to watch
- [Managed Postgres](docs/managed-postgres.md): the setup on a managed service; Neon and Supabase, as tried
- [Files in S3-compatible storage](docs/signed-urls.md): signed URLs handed out only after the row was read
- [Error codes](docs/errors/README.md): every mistake's code, what it means and the same mistake fixed
- [Playground](playground/README.md): the compiler and Postgres in the browser, nothing installed
